The 2027 Aliner Classic LXE Packs a Bathroom Into "One of the Smallest Trailers" Out There
14 photos
Photo: Aliner
Compact and lightweight, highly garageable, easy to set up, yet packed with everything a pair of adventurers would need – surely that sounds like that fabled RV/travel trailer that is about as real as glitter-pooping unicorns. The Aliner Classic LXE is no unicorn, glitter or no glitter, but it does come close to being the perfect camper.
U.S.-based camper specialist Aliner has long dubbed itself "America's trusted camper brand since 1984," and for once, there are no factual objections to it. Aliner has been around for decades and their popularity seems to hold steady, if not actually boom as the years pass. The same goes for the feedback they get for their product, so they're definitely doing something right.
Their Aliner Classic LXE is a good example of what that thing is that they're doing so right.
Aliner could also take credit for making collapsible travel trailers mainstream, though they stop short of that. Their approach to the perfect short-vacation RV has always been the hybrid, collapsible travel trailer, which you can get either in standard configuration or with extra bells and whistles for more comfort.
Photo: Aliner The Classic LXE comes pre-loaded with those, so it's a complete solution in and of itself. Aliner packs HVAC , hot water, a nice galley, and even a wet bathroom inside "one of the smallest trailers on the market," so that explains its lasting appeal.
The LXE nameplate has been present in the Aliner catalog since the late '90s, but the Classic LXE iteration is more recent. It stands for "Luxury Edition/Executive," signaling that this is a Classic trailer with everything you need already included.
The Classic sub-series falls under the A-Frame lineup in the Aliner catalog, so that tells you that this is a collapsible trailer that pitches at camp in an A-frame shape. You also get an oversized dormer on the front and a smaller one on the back, and you have the option to make the front one a hard wall if you want a bit more sturdiness.
Photo: Aliner The Classic LXE travels compact , much like a boxy cargo trailer. At camp, in under 30 minutes, a single person will open the hinged panels on that box, pitching a camper that looks like an odd tent. Unlike a tent, though, this one has hard-sided fiberglass walls, actual sliding windows, a solid roof, an aluminum frame, and more importantly, it sits at least 14 inches off the ground.
Though Aliner says that this is a complete, self-contained RV solution, the Classic XLE is an upgrade to tent camping – but it's the nicest one around. It's something to get you off the ground, out of the cold or the heat, and under a dry roof, while you enjoy the basic creature comforts.
The Classic XLE rides on a single axle and coming in at 15 feet (4.5 meters) in total length and a width of 78 inches (198 cm). It's just 64 inches (162 cm) high when it's closed for transport, "growing" to as much as 121 inches (307 cm) at camp on the standard 14-inch aluminum wheels and 124 inches (315 cm) if you go for the optional offroad configuration with 15-inch wheels and offroad tires.
Photo: Aliner It's highly garageable and very easy to maneuver or tow, Aliner points out. At 1,930 lbs (875 kg) of dry weight, 180 lbs (82 kg) of hitch weight, and a gross weight of 3,000 lbs (1,361 kg), it's also compatible with a wide range of towing vehicles.
Aliner describes it as "true self-contained comfort without the bulk," and that becomes obvious once you step inside. This is a two-person camper, with a large queen bed available at the back when you drop the table and join the sofa to the side benches, a nice galley on the off-side, and a wet bathroom module on the campside.
If you're not unfamiliar to Aliners , you probably know how these "modules" look. It's a small block with a large counter, which lifts to reveal a shower and a cassette toilet. The counter becomes a hard wall, and you also get a shower to go around the shower.
Photo: Aliner It's obviously not the most elegant option around, but it is a bathroom inside a 15-footer.
The LXE also comes standard with an 18,000-BTU furnace, an AC unit with a heat pump mounted under one of the benches, a water heater that services the galley, the shower module, and the outside shower, and a kitchen that really lacks for nothing given its dimensions. It comes standard with a two-burner Euro-style flush-mounted gas cooktop under a glass cover, a sink under a separate cover, a microwave, and a 12V fridge.
Because of its highest selling point, the transformational capability , the Classic LXE doesn't offer storage in the upper part, which has to fold down for transport. Storage options throughout the camper will be limited, and that's probably also the camper's weakest point.
Photo: Aliner Standard features also include opening windows on all four walls, a multi-speed fan in the ceiling to keep the air moving, four stabilizer jacks, a bike rack receiver, and an 11-gallon (41.6-liter) tank for freshwater. Aliner also includes a gas connection on the outside, a railing for a table, an outside storage compartment, power outlets inside and out, and LED lights inside and out.
Options include two LP tanks with a hard cover, a hard wall for the front dormer, a solar panel on the same dormer, high wind lift assist that will add extra strength to the camper, and the lift kit with the bigger wheels and offroad tires.
Sale prices depend on equipment and options, but also on the dealer you get your unit from, averaging around $30,000 – give or take a couple thousand of dollars.
